name: Preamble
text: THIS AGREEMENT AND DECLARATION OF TRUST, adopted as of February 20, 1956, and amended and restated, effective as of the September 1, 1993, establishing the Newspaper and’ Mail Deliverers’ -- Publishers’ Pension Fund (the "Fund" or "Plan"), by and among (a) The Publishers’ Association of New York City (the "Association"), acting on behalf of employers in the newspaper delivery industry who are members of the Association, and such other employers which from time. to time become contributing employers hereunder, and their successors and assigns (collectively, the “Employers") and The Newspaper and Mail Deliverers’ Union of New York and Vicinity and its affiliates and their successors and assigns (collectively, the "tnion"), and (b) the following individuals: JOSEPH COTTER, BARBARA KALISH, PATRICK LAGAN, ROBERT NUSSPICKLE, and FRANK SPARACINO, and their successors and assigns (such persons, and others who from time to time are designated hereunder, being hereinafter collectively referred to as the "Trustees" of the Fund).

name: Recital - Collective Bargaining Agreements
text: WHEREAS, the Union and the Employers have executed, and may from time to time hereafter execute, collective bargaining agreements ("Collective Bargaining Agreements") which, among other things, establish the Plan and require periodic Employer contributions to it;

name: Recital - Trust Agreement contemplated
text: WHEREAS, the Collective Bargaining Agreements contenplate that the Union and the Association will execute a Trust Agreement and appoint Trustees;

name: Recital - Purpose of Fund
text: WHEREAS, to effectuate the aforesaid purpose, this Agreement and Declaration of Trust is made and shall be known as the Newspaper and Mail Deliverers’ -- Publishers’ Pension Fund (the "Trust," "Fund" or "Trust Fund") to be used for the exclusive purpose of providing pension and retirement benefits to certain employees of the Employers ("Covered Employees") and their dependents or beneficiaries (the "Beneficiaries") eligible to participate in the Plan;

name: Recital - Desire to amend and restate
text: WHEREAS, the Trustees now desire to amend and restate the existing agreement and declaration of trust establishing the Fund, dated February 20, 1956 as amended on June 1, 1976 and from time to time thereafter; and

name: Recital - Authority to amend
text: WHEREAS, Paragraph 18 of the Trust Agreement authorizes the Trustees to amend the provisions of the Trust Agreement.

name: 5.10 Bonding
text: 5.10 Bonding. Any person required to be bonded under the provisions of ERISA, including without limitation the Trustees, Administrator, Investment Managers, Custodians (and any other employees, agents or other representatives of the Trust handling monies, Securities and negotiable paper on behalf of the Trust or otherwise entrusted with any portion of the Trust Fund), shall be bonded under a fidelity bond issued by a reputable insurance carrier in the amount required by Section 412 of ERISA. The Board shall, in its sole discretion, have the authority to require the bonding of any other employee of the Trust and to require bonds above the minimum amount. The cost of premiums for such bonds shall be paid out of the Trust Fund.

name: 6.1 Officers
text: 6.1 Officers. (a) The term of Fund officers shall commence on the date of their election and continues until their successors are elected. At all times, the Chairman of the Fund shall be a Union Trustee and the Secretary of the Fund shall be an Employer Trustee. (b) The Chairman shall preside over meetings of the Board and, additionally, shall perform such other duties as the Board may direct.

name: 6.2 Calling of Meetings
text: 6.2 Calling of Meetings. (a) There shall be at least four regular quarterly meetings of the Trustees each year, the time of such meetings to be determined by the Trustees. (b) Special meetings may be called by the Chairman or Secretary or by any four Trustees at any time by giving at least five (5) days advance written notice of the time and place of such meeting to all other Trustees. (c) Meetings may be held at any time, with proper advance notice (as prescribed by either paragraph (a) or (b) above), by telephone conference. (d) Meetings of the Trustees may also be held at any time, without notice, in person or by telephone conference; provided, that all the Trustees consent thereto. (e) The place of all regular and special meetings shall be determined by the Trustees.

name: 6.3 Quorum
text: 6.3 Quorum. A quorum for the transaction of business at any regular or special meeting of the Trustees shall consist of two Union Trustees and two Employer Trustees.

text: 9.3 Mode of Payment. All contributions shall be payable to the "Newspaper and Mail Deliverers’ -- Publishers’ Pension Fund," and shall be paid in the manner and form prescribed by the Board.

name: 9.4 Failure to Make Employer Contributions
text: 9.4 Failure to Make Employer Contributions. (a) The failure of any Employer to make Employer contributions to the Trust Fund when due shall not relieve any other Employer of its obligation to make Employer contributions. The costs and expenses incurred in the collection of Employer contributions shall be paid from the Fund. Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, upon the failure of any Employer to make Employer contributions to the Trust Fund required by the Plan, the Trust Fund or a Collective Bargaining Agreement, within ten (10) days after such payments are due and payable, the Board (or its counsel or other duly authorized designee) may compel and enforce payment in any manner it deems proper (including, without limitation, the assessment of interest, at a rate calculated in accordance with Section 9.5, from the date such payments first became due and payable). (b) In addition, the Board may require a delinquent Employer to pay a liquidated damage penalty equal to the greater of interest on, or twenty percent of, the unpaid contributions, plus all costs and expenses incurred by the Trustees arising out of the collection of such delinquent Employer contributions (including, without limitation, court costs and attor- neys’ fees).

text: (b) A delinquent Employer shall be liable for any expenses incurred in effectuating such payment (including, but not limited to, arbitration expenses, counsel fees, court costs, and interest at a rate of 18 percent per annum).

text: “9,10 Arbitration of Withdrawal Liability Disputes. . Any and all claims by third parties (including Employers) against the Trust Fund concerning the assessment by the Trust Fund of withdrawal liability under Sections 4201 through 4219 of ERISA .. which cannot. be resolved between the claimant and the Trust Fund shall not become the subject of litigation in the courts (either State or Federal), but shall be subject to determination only by arbitration before an arbitrator designated by the American Arbitration Association (the "AAA") in accordance with its Multi- Employer Pension Plan Arbitration Rules for Withdrawal Liability Disputes.
